source.title: Language Models are Homer Simpson! Safety Re-Alignment of Fine-tuned Language Models through Task Arithmetic
source.authors: Rishabh Bhardwaj; Do Duc Anh; Soujanya Poria

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign supervised fine-tuning raises harmful-response rates, using GPT-4-judged unsafety scores across fine-tuning datasets and safety benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports results for adding a safety vector and for DARE, but those interventions do not test the listed claim versions. Those results are not cataloged as rows. Table values are mapped using the table headings and are reported separately by fine-tuning method, dataset, and evaluation benchmark.
record.test_reason: Benign SFT (Alpaca in Chinese/Hindi/English, CodeAlpaca, GSM8K) of Llama-2-7B-Chat, with GPT-4-judged unsafety on four harmful-question benchmarks against the uncompromised model, directly bears on V2. The RESTA/DARE results are the paper's own mitigation and are not rows.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The main conclusion is that RESTA (adding a safety vector, optionally with DARE) cuts fine-tuned models' unsafety from 17.86% to 4.57% with minimal performance loss and generalizes across benchmarks and languages. That benign SFT compromises Llama-2 is shown, but as the motivating observation rather than the headline.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates ordinary domain-specific SFT and GPT-4-judged harmfulness across datasets and benchmarks; it does not reproduce the cited fine-tuning study's harmful-example intervention. The paper additionally proposes safety-vector addition and DARE.
record.method_sensitivity: Unsafety scores vary across fine-tuning dataset, PEFT versus Full-FT, benchmark, and evaluation language. The paper also states that DARE's effectiveness may depend on model size, learning rate, and SFT domain.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Experiments use Llama-2-7B-Chat; the authors note they did not extensively evaluate hyperparameters or larger models. GPT-4 refusals to judge some responses were omitted from score computation, and uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the listed versions were omitted. Table entries for SFT+DARE and SFT+RESTA were left out because they evaluate the paper's proposed recovery interventions rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Carefully selected benign data, such as identity-shift or gradient-selected examples. Models other than Llama-2-7B-Chat. Effect of dataset size or epochs.
A 100-example harmful QA unalignment is used to build the safety vector, but no unsafety score for that model is reported.
Not tested; the safety vector and DARE are mitigation tools, not a localization test.

missing.what: Per-category CatQA unsafety for base, SFT and RESTA (11 harm categories), given only as a figure

Full-FT averages in Tables 4 and 5 (12.03, 4.84) do not match the mean of the five listed dataset values (16.49, 5.69). The per-dataset values may be misaligned in the source; researchers should check the original PDF.

record.verdict_notes: Single model (Llama-2-7B-Chat), GPT-4 judge, no uncertainty reported, and GPT-4 refusals to judge are dropped. Non-English Alpaca sets are mixed with 50K English examples. The reader's Table 2 Full-FT values were shifted one column (r06-r10 corrected). Hindi under Full-FT shows little or no erosion on three of four benchmarks. The multilingual CatQA baselines are already elevated (10.2, 15.3).

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report harmful-response rates after fine-tuning on harmful examples as the intervention of interest.
Does not test carefully selected benign examples as a separate category; evaluates fine-tuning on the listed language, code, and math datasets.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test.
DARE drops and rescales fine-tuning delta parameters, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test why safety would be shallow.
Does not train or evaluate a method intended to deepen safety beyond the first response tokens.
